title: "Setup"

## Why a repository at all

GitHub hosts code, data, and documents on the web. Four reasons it matters for research:

- **Transparency** — the work is open to inspection.
- **Reproducibility** — others can recreate and extend your analysis.
- **Collaboration** — several people contribute to one project without emailing files.
- **Version control** — every change is tracked, and reverting is trivial.

::: {.note}
[And for working with agents]{.note-head}
An agent edits files in place. The repository is what makes that safe: you can see
exactly what changed (`git diff`) and undo it (`git restore`). Without version control,
you are letting a confident stranger type into your manuscript.
:::

## What a repository looks like

A repository is a folder with your code, data, documentation, and the complete history
of changes. This one:

```
UNM_Workshop/
├── AGENTS.md              the brief every AI agent reads
├── CLAUDE.md              one line: @AGENTS.md
├── data/
│   ├── wss_2020_2024.csv  analysis file (read-only)
│   └── wss_clean.rds      built by R/01_recode.R
├── codebooks/             2020 & 2024 survey codebooks (PDF)
├── R/
│   ├── functions.R        pure helpers, shared and unit-tested
│   ├── 00_build_data.R    raw Stata → csv (instructor only)
│   ├── 01_recode.R        all recoding lives here
│   └── 02_analysis.R      models and figures → output/
├── app/app.R              Shiny explorer
├── tests/testthat/        test-unit-* and test-integration-*
├── slides/                workshop slides (Quarto revealjs)
└── .devcontainer/         one-click Codespace
```

Numbered scripts, one job each, strict order. **Recodes never live in analysis
scripts** — that single rule is what keeps four people and an agent from quietly
disagreeing about what `latino` means.

## GitHub

1. Create an account at <https://github.com>. Students and faculty: apply for
   [GitHub Education](https://education.github.com) — it includes free Copilot Pro.
2. The repository is public — you do not need to be added to anything. Clone it to read
   and run it — that is all today needs (see [Git workflow](03-git.qmd)).
3. Install Git: macOS `xcode-select --install`; Windows <https://git-scm.com>.
4. Identify yourself once:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@unm.edu"
```

5. Authenticate: install the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com), then:

```bash
gh auth login
gh auth status      # confirm
```

## R and RStudio

- Work from the **terminal** for Git commands. In RStudio:
  **Tools → Terminal → New Terminal**.
- The **Git** tab gives you the same operations by point-and-click. The commands are
  identical underneath, and the terminal is what you can explain to a collaborator —
  or to an agent.
- Open `UNM_Workshop.Rproj` so that relative paths (`data/wss_clean.rds`) resolve.

## Copilot

- **VS Code** → Extensions → **GitHub Copilot** + **GitHub Copilot Chat** → sign in.
- **RStudio** → *Tools → Global Options → Copilot → Enable*.
- Copilot reads `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which here points at `AGENTS.md`.

## Claude Code

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code    # or: brew install claude-code
cd UNM_Workshop
claude
```

Requires a Claude Pro/Max account or an API key. There is also a VS Code extension —
search "Claude Code". On first run, try `/init` and read what it writes about this
project.

## No local setup? Use a Codespace

On the repository page: **Code → Codespaces → Create codespace on main**.

The container (`.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`) installs R and tidyverse, RStudio
Server on port 8787, Quarto, Copilot, and Claude Code — in a browser tab, identical for
everyone in the room.

[![Open in Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop)

::: {.warn}
[Housekeeping]{.warn-head}
The free tier is 60 core-hours a month. **Stop your codespace when you are done** — it
bills while it idles.
:::

::: {.turn}
[Follow along, if you like]{.turn-head}
1. Start a codespace, or clone the repo locally.
2. Run `gh auth status` — are you signed in?
3. Start `claude`, run `/init`, and read the result against `AGENTS.md`.
:::
